newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks at new high, but gains seen slowing.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks at new high, but gains seen slowing.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares continued mostly strong on Tuesday but brokers said the bourse's two-week bull-run was likely to slow down soon as some counters were now overpriced.
"The market was firm today but we are seeing a bit of selling, mainly from foreigners," one broker said.
"We might see it slowing down soon because some shares are overpriced," he said.
The key industrial index rose 35.10 points to close at 8,086.94, a new all time high.
It was pushed higher largely by cigarette manufacturer Rothmans' 300-cent leap to 3,800, hotel and supermarkets group Meikles' 250-cent surge to 3,250 and winery Cairns' 100-cent rise to 1,100.
Clothing and furniture retailer Tedco's gained 80 cents to 610, cement producer Circle rose 50 cents to 650 and sugar cane grower Hippo added 10 cents to 900.

A handful of counters bucked the trend with blue-chip conglomerate Delta dropping 100 cents to 3,200, Alloys shedding 25 cents to 900 while construction firm J and F at 200, pork processor Colcom at 340 and agricultural products company Acacia at 260 all traded 10 cents off.

In minings, nickel producer Bindura at 1,050 and Wankie Colliery at 365 were both unchanged in reasonable turnover while gold company Ashanti slid 300 cents to 13,800. Falgold was the only winner, adding 10 cents to 140.
The mining index edged 2.08 points up to 1,236.96.
